q: Who is credited with designing Fallingwater?
n: Fallingwater, cantilevered over a waterfall in rural Pennsylvania, is considered Wright's masterwork of organic architecture, fusing the house with its natural site.

q: Together with Henry-Russell Hitchcock, which architect coined the term 'International Style'?
n: Johnson and historian Henry-Russell Hitchcock coined ‘International Style’ for their landmark 1932 MoMA exhibition documenting the new European modernist architecture.

q: Which architect earned the title 'Father of Skyscrapers'?
n: Sullivan, mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright and a leader of the Chicago School, pioneered early steel-frame tall buildings and coined ‘form follows function,’ earning him the title ‘Father of Skyscrapers.’

q: Which art movement is defined by fragmenting subjects into geometric planes and shapes?
n: Cubism, developed by Picasso and Braque, breaks subjects into geometric planes viewed from multiple angles at once.

q: Who invented the geodesic dome, built on the principle of the space frame?
n: Fuller popularized the geodesic dome, a lightweight shell built from a triangulated space frame that distributes structural loads evenly across its surface.

q: Which 1920s to 1930s style favors simple, clean, streamlined shapes with ornament that is geometric or stylized from natural forms?
n: Art Deco favored simple, clean, streamlined forms with geometric or stylized ornament — a deliberate departure from Art Nouveau's flowing organic lines.

q: Which style is a lavish, heavily ornamented classical tradition?
n: Beaux-Arts, taught at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, is a grand, heavily ornamented classical style built on symmetry and elaborate detailing.

q: Which building best exemplifies Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture?
n: Villa Savoye is the clearest built demonstration of Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture: pilotis, free plan, free façade, ribbon windows, and roof garden.

q: Which early 20th-century movement in art and architecture aimed to evoke inner feeling and extreme emotion, producing buildings that stood apart from their surroundings?
n: Expressionist buildings used dramatic, emotionally charged forms — often distorted or sculptural — to stand apart from their surroundings and evoke inner feeling.

q: Juan Arellano's Central Post Office building exemplifies which style?
ref: Juan Arellano — Manila Central Post Office, 1926
n: Arellano's Central Post Office, with its symmetrical colonnaded façade, is a landmark of Neoclassical design in the Philippines.

q: Which style is marked chiefly by swirling 'whiplash' curves, with ornament and color drawn from plants, flowers, and animals?
n: Art Nouveau is defined by sinuous, asymmetrical ‘whiplash’ curves drawn from plant and animal forms, applied to both ornament and structure.

q: Who was among the founders of Art Nouveau in the 1890s, known for the central stair hall of the Hotel Tassel in Brussels?
n: Horta's Hôtel Tassel, with its glass-and-iron stairwell, is regarded as the first fully realized Art Nouveau building and established Horta as a founder of the style.

q: Left unfinished by 'God's Architect,' which structure is considered one of the longest-running construction projects in the world?
n: Gaudí, known as ‘God's Architect,’ left the Sagrada Família unfinished at his death in 1926; still under construction, it is one of the longest-running building projects in history.

q: Simple, clean shapes with a streamlined look are the defining traits of which style?
n: Simple, clean, streamlined shapes with minimal geometric ornament define Art Deco, distinguishing it from the heavier historicist styles that preceded it.

q: The Manila Metropolitan Theater (the Met), a fine local example of this style, was designed by which architect?
n: The Met is one of the finest Art Deco buildings in the Philippines, designed by Juan Arellano, who wove tropical and Filipino decorative motifs into the style.

q: Home to the 'Father of Skyscrapers' and his major contributions, which city is regarded as the birthplace of the skyscraper?
n: Chicago's rapid rebuilding after the 1871 fire, combined with Louis Sullivan's steel-frame innovations, made the city the birthplace of the modern skyscraper.

q: Introduced by Frank Lloyd Wright and best exemplified by the Robie House in Chicago, what is this Midwestern American style called?
ref: Frank Lloyd Wright — Prairie Style, Robie House, 1910
n: The Prairie Style, developed by Wright in the American Midwest, emphasized long horizontal lines echoing the flat prairie landscape; the Robie House in Chicago is its best-known example.

q: Which architect compared a house to a flower pot, an organic metaphor about a building's relation to its site?
n: Wright reached for organic metaphors like this to argue that a house should grow naturally out of, and stay rooted to, its site — a core idea of his organic architecture.

q: Which style is often called minimalist for stripping away ornament and reducing a building to its most basic structural elements?
n: The International Style, formalized by Hitchcock and Johnson, stripped buildings to essential structure: flat surfaces, open volumes, and an absence of applied ornament.

q: Which architect said, 'Architecture begins where engineering ends'?
n: Gropius, founder of the Bauhaus, used this line to argue that architecture's spatial and aesthetic ambitions extend beyond what structural engineering alone can achieve.

q: The Farnsworth House exemplifies a mature phase of modern architecture that this architect termed _________.
ref: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe — Farnsworth House, 1951
n: Mies called his mature minimalist approach — an exposed structural frame (‘bones’) wrapped in glass (‘skin’) — ‘skin-and-bones’ architecture.

q: Who declared that 'a house is a machine for living in'?
n: This famous line from Le Corbusier's ‘Towards a New Architecture’ framed the modern house as a rationally engineered object designed purely for efficient living.

q: All but one of these architects are known for the raw-concrete Beton Brut (Brutalist) style. Which one is the exception?
ref: Pablo Antonio — not associated with Béton Brut
n: Le Corbusier, Marcel Breuer, and Leandro Locsin all produced major works in raw-concrete Béton Brut (Brutalist) style; Pablo Antonio worked mainly in Art Deco and early Philippine modernism.

q: Exposing support beams, ductwork, and other functional elements on a building's exterior to keep the interior open and adaptable is the mark of high-tech architecture. What are such buildings often called?
n: High-tech buildings that expose structural and service elements — ducts, pipes, beams — on the exterior are nicknamed ‘Bowellism,’ as if the building's services were turned inside-out.

q: What is the term for a trademark technique of exposing a building's service systems in plain view?
n: This technique of displaying a building's mechanical ‘guts’ on the outside is called Bowellism, famously used by Richard Rogers at the Pompidou Centre and Lloyd's of London.

q: Who pioneered innovative tensile membrane structures?
n: Frei Otto pioneered lightweight tensile membrane structures, most famously the tent-like roof of the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972).

q: All of these are noted Post-Modernist architects except one. Which is the exception?
n: Michael Graves, Robert Venturi, and Philip Johnson (in his later work) are leading Post-Modernists; Erich Mendelsohn belongs to the earlier 1920s Expressionist movement.

q: Who designed the Portland Building?
n: Graves's Portland Building, with its colorful, ornamented, classically referenced façade, is considered one of the first major Post-Modern civic buildings.

q: Which building served as a built demonstration of the 'complexities and contradictions' found in modern architecture?
n: Venturi designed this house for his mother as a built manifesto for his book ‘Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture,’ challenging modernist orthodoxy.

q: Designed by the very first Pritzker Prize laureate, which building became an icon of Post-Modernism?
n: Philip Johnson, the first-ever Pritzker Prize laureate (1979), designed the AT&T Building with its famous broken-pediment ‘Chippendale’ top, an icon of Post-Modernism.

q: Who quipped that 'architecture is the art of how to waste space'?
n: Johnson's wry remark captures the Post-Modern embrace of generous, even excessive, space and ornament as expressive tools rather than strictly functional ones.

q: All but one of these buildings are works of I. M. Pei. Which one is the exception?
o: Rock and Roll hall of Fame
n: The Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts is Le Corbusier's only building in North America; the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Dallas City Hall, and the Luce Memorial Chapel are all I. M. Pei projects.

q: Who held that function should influence but not dictate form?
n: Saarinen argued that function should inform architectural form without rigidly dictating it, allowing for the expressive, sculptural shapes seen in works like the TWA Flight Center.

q: Which movement deliberately violates the cubes and right angles characteristic of modernism?
n: Deconstructivist architects deliberately fragment and destabilize modernism's orthogonal geometry, producing dynamic, seemingly unstable forms.

q: Which of these architects is NOT associated with Deconstructivism?
n: Frank Gehry, Zaha Hadid, and Rem Koolhaas are core Deconstructivist figures; Alvar Aalto belongs to an earlier generation of humanist modernism.

q: All of these architects received the National Artist Award for Architecture except one. Who is the exception?
ref: Tomas Mapua — not a National Artist
n: Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and Ildefonso P. Santos all received the National Artist for Architecture award; Tomas Mapua, the first licensed Filipino architect and founder of the country's first architecture school, was never named one.

q: Who designed the PBCom Tower in Makati?
n: Formoso's firm, GF & Partners, designed the PBCom Tower, which was the tallest building in the Philippines from 2000 to 2017.

q: Which architect designed both the Aglipayan Church in Manila and the PhilamLife Building?
n: Carlos Arguelles designed the landmark PhilamLife Building on UN Avenue, known for its folded-plate concrete roof, along with the Aglipayan Church in Manila.

q: Who designed the Philippine Heart Center and the GSIS Building?
ref: Jorge Ramos — Philippine Heart Center & GSIS Building
n: Jorge Ramos designed both the Philippine Heart Center (1975) and the GSIS Building (1982) in the Brutalist style typical of major government commissions of the Marcos era.

q: Who designed the Regina and Perez Buildings in Manila?
o: Antonio T. Luna de San Pedro
ref: Andrés Luna de San Pedro — Regina & Perez-Samanillo Buildings, Escolta
n: Andrés Luna de San Pedro, son of painter Juan Luna, designed both the Art Deco Perez-Samanillo Building and the Beaux-Arts Regina Building that face each other along Escolta, Manila.

q: Who supervised and carried out the master plans for Manila and Baguio that had been prepared by another architect?
n: Daniel Burnham prepared the master plans for Manila and Baguio, but William E. Parsons, appointed consulting architect, stayed on to supervise and carry them out.

q: Who received the National Artist Award for Architecture in 1990?
n: Leandro Locsin was named National Artist for Architecture in 1990, honored for landmark works including the Cultural Center of the Philippines and the Tanghalang Pambansa.

q: Which building below is NOT a work of Francisco Manosa?
ref: Francisco Mañosa — not the Meralco Building
n: Mañosa is known for the Coconut Palace, the San Miguel Corporation head office, and Amanpulo, all rooted in his ‘Filipino architecture’ philosophy; the Meralco Building was not among his designs.

q: Who designed the Baclaran Church and the Insular Life Building?
ref: Cesar Concio — Redemptorist (Baclaran) Church & Insular Life Building
n: Cesar Concio designed both the Redemptorist Church, popularly known as Baclaran Church, and the Insular Life Building in Makati.

q: All but one of these are Leandro Locsin designs within the CCP Complex. Which one is the exception?
ref: Froilan Hong — Manila Film Center, not by Locsin
n: Locsin designed the Cultural Center of the Philippines, Tanghalang Francisco Balagtas, and the Philippine International Convention Center; the Manila Film Center, though within the same complex, was designed by Froilan Hong.
